segments.t: In the hallway at ASK, Andréa confronts Gabriel after catching him flirting with her new client. She lays down the firm's strict rules regarding professional boundaries and client relationships. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Voilà la règle numéro un ici.
On ne drague jamais les clients. Jamais.
J'offrais juste un accueil très chaleureux.
Quel mal ça peut faire?
C'est un talent brut magnifique.
Il m'a fallu des mois pour obtenir ce rendez-vous.
Tous les agents de Paris la veulent.
J'ai fait tout le travail parce que je crois en elle.
Je ne veux pas que tu fasses tout rater.
Tu dragues aussi tes clients, Andréa.
Dis-moi que tu n'es pas attirée par elle.
Bien sûr que si, sinon je ne voudrais pas la représenter.
Mais je ne veux pas coucher avec elle.
C'est la grande différence entre toi et moi.
Je fais attention, ne t'inquiète pas.
Reste loin d'elle, c'est tout ce que je te demande.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Voilà la règle numéro un ici.
'Here is rule number one here.' Andréa establishes the fundamental agency principle. The presentative 'here is' introduces 'the' with authority.
On ne drague jamais les clients. Jamais.
'We never flirt with clients. Never.' Andréa states the ethical boundary emphatically. Listen for the expression meaning 'not', which leads naturally into 'never'.
J'offrais juste un accueil très chaleureux.
'I was just offering a very warm welcome.' Gabriel minimizes his playful charm. The adjective meaning 'warm' agrees in gender and number with masculine noun 'welcome'.
Quel mal ça peut faire?
'What harm can it do?' Gabriel questions the strict prohibition casually. The interrogative determiner 'what' agrees with the masculine noun 'harm'.
C'est un talent brut magnifique.
'She is a magnificent raw talent.' Andréa defends her new client's artistic promise. Notice how the verb for 'she is' leads straight into 'talent'.
Il m'a fallu des mois pour obtenir ce rendez-vous.
'It took me months to get this meeting.' Andréa emphasizes her patient effort. Notice how the verb for 'took me' leads straight into 'meeting'.
Tous les agents de Paris la veulent.
'Every agent in Paris wants her.' Andréa underscores the intense competition. The plural determiner 'all' precedes the noun 'agents'.
J'ai fait tout le travail parce que je crois en elle.
'I did all the work because I believe in her.' Andréa asserts her professional dedication. Andréa pairs the verb meaning 'I have' with the noun for 'work'.
Je ne veux pas que tu fasses tout rater.
'I do not want you to ruin everything.' Andréa warns against reckless interference. Andréa opens with the word for 'not' and lands on 'fail' at the close.
Tu dragues aussi tes clients, Andréa.
'You flirt with your clients too, Andréa.' Gabriel deflects the criticism playfully. Gabriel pairs the verb meaning 'flirt with' with the noun for 'client'.
Dis-moi que tu n'es pas attirée par elle.
'Tell me you are not attracted to her.' Gabriel challenges her personal motives. Gabriel gives a direct imperative using the verb for 'tell me'.
Bien sûr que si, sinon je ne voudrais pas la représenter.
'Of course I am, otherwise I would not want to represent her.' Andréa readily concedes. The affirmative response 'of course' contradicts a negative question.
Mais je ne veux pas coucher avec elle.
'But I do not want to sleep with her.' Andréa draws a sharp line between attraction and action. The colloquial infinitive 'to sleep with' denotes sleeping with someone.
C'est la grande différence entre toi et moi.
'That is the big difference between you and me.' Andréa summarizes her professional discipline. Listen for the expression meaning 'that is', which leads naturally into 'difference'.
Je fais attention, ne t'inquiète pas.
'I am being careful, do not worry.' Gabriel attempts to reassure his colleague. The key word here means 'make', paired with 'not' to make the point clear.
Reste loin d'elle, c'est tout ce que je te demande.

'Stay away from her, that is all I ask of you.' Andréa delivers her final firm instruction. The relative structure 'that' functions as the object of 'I'. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.

Andréa lays down the law on agency conduct: romantic entanglements with clients are strictly forbidden. Gabriel promises to behave, but his romantic impulses remain hard to tame. See you in the next scene.
